# `cali_user_location`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Recompute the star-horizon calibration location offsets, optionally from a supplied RA/Dec pair, and report them.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (strict, 64-bit and 32-bit builds; offset cache replacement and logging) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe6da0 (64-bit build); offset helpers and PrintClibLoc (64-bit build) |

Optionally takes ra and dec (object or positional). If a coordinate pair parsed and the device calibration mode (calib_location) is 1 and the user location loads, the device replaces its in-memory location-offset pair; if the pair is missing or invalid it queries the previous pair instead, with no error. RA is in hours and Dec in degrees. The result always has calib_location and conditionally the offset arrays; effect_offset_deg can appear twice. calib_location is a mode (1 enables goto location calibration, 2 enables the three-point polar-alignment offset, any other value disables both). The effects are cached calculations; no settings persistence or motion is shown.

Side effects: May replace the in-memory calibration location offset pair and refresh the cached user location and time; logs the calculation. Full command-socket calls also incur the shared diagnostic (logging) writes; this is why the strict grade is MUTATOR even for the read-only calls.

Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

| `params` | object\|array | no | - | Optional pair of numbers. Accepted as an object with ra and dec, or positionally as [ra, dec]. If either value is missing, null or not a number, the handler proceeds with no coordinate pair and reports no error. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No handler-specific error is reachable; helper failures only suppress the conditional arrays.

## Example

Request, query-previous:

```json
{"id":30,"method":"cali_user_location"}
```

Request, with-pair:

```json
{"id":31,"method":"cali_user_location","params":{"ra":5.5,"dec":22.0}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"cali_user_location","result":{"calib_location":1,"offset_deg":[0.5,-0.25]},"code":0,"id":31}
```
